detail.explanation: A changed run only means something if the unchanged run repeats. The normal run was recorded twice, and the comparison file reports the two recordings identical: same console lines, same events, same value in all 24 registers of all four hash banks. Four fields are allowed to vary and are named in each recording: the recording time, the run name and two timings. The pilots in this section were made before any prediction existed and are not counted; the counted experiments were each run once, after their prediction was committed.

status_mismatch.specification: For an image whose signature is not valid, the description of the load service names the security violation status. The access denied status appears only in its status table, for an image that platform policy prohibits from being loaded.
status_mismatch.reading: The two do not match, and no sentence is broken: both statuses are defined, and no sentence says which one a platform must use. The choice is the platform's.
status_mismatch.limit: The recording holds the printed words, not the returned status value. The table in which firmware records a refused image was not read from the machine.

detail.explanation: The signature on the loader covers a hash of its content, so one changed byte means the signature no longer matches. Firmware printed that it failed to load the boot option, never printed that it started it, and none of the loader's own lines appear. The two event logs are the same up to event 24 and differ from event 25: the normal run records the authorising record, the loader's measurement and the two exit records, and the changed run records none of them. Registers 4, 5 and 7 differ in all four hash banks, and every other register is the same.
not_shown: Whether a refused loader must be left out of the TPM record is not something UEFI 2.11 says. The Trusted Computing Group document that would define it has not been read for this project.

claims.text: The changed run differs from the normal run by one byte of the loader's data: offset 2142, value 65 changed to 66, in the .data section.
This run is a pilot: it was made before any prediction was committed.
In the normal run the loader printed that it had started.
In the changed run firmware printed that it failed to load the boot option, with the words Access Denied.
In the changed run firmware never printed that it was starting the boot option, and no line from the loader appears.
The recorded outcome is accepted for the normal run and refused for the changed run.
The first event that differs is event 25. Events 1 to 24 are the same in both runs.
Event 25 is placed at stop 6, loading and verifying the loader. That placement is this project's own mapping.
Registers 4, 5 and 7 differ between the two runs in all four hash banks. Every other register is the same.
Four events are only in the normal run: the authorising record in register 7, the loader's measurement in register 4, and two exit records in register 5.
Two events are only in the changed run, both in register 4: a return from the boot option and a second call of a boot option.
In the normal run the digest of the loader's measurement equals the digest the loader was signed over.
This firmware logged no measurement of the refused loader: the changed loader's signing digest is not among the 26 event digests of the changed run.

claims.text: A signature is checked against a hash that must be computed exactly as it was when the image was signed.

To pass, the allowed list must hold the image's hash or a certificate that verifies its signature. A changed byte changes the hash, so by this project's reading the changed loader meets neither condition.
An image that fails the check is not started, and information about it is placed in a table kept by firmware.
When the image that fails is an operating system loader, the next boot option is selected.

Which status the load service returns for a failed signature check is left to the platform. The description names the security violation status for an invalid signature; the access denied status is the table row for an image that platform policy prohibits from loading.
The decision to launch an image is left to the firmware: it decides on the match or on its own policy.
